summary: No release-blocking issues: the search query is fully parameterised, the sort is chosen from a fixed allow-list, and the page offset is clamped. Minor hardening only (reject non-numeric page values and escape LIKE wildcards in the search term).

No code defect found, but the audit omits the payment-verification check that the repository's release test suite defines, so a mandatory check has no evidence. The GO cannot be recorded until that check is run against the release commit.

GET /projects trusts the client-supplied x-org-id header and never checks it against res.locals.user.orgIds, so any signed-in user can read another organisation's projects and budgets (IDOR / tenant isolation failure).

No release-blocking issues: RLS is enabled with owner-scoped policies for every operation, and the update policy's USING clause also applies to the new row, so owner_id cannot be reassigned. saveNote silently succeeds when no row matches, which is worth handling but not a blocker.

The only finding (AG-007, no per-account login rate limit, medium) is formally accepted with an owner, approver, compensating IP rate limiting at the edge and a two-week fix date. All critical checks pass at the audited commit, and the AI-permissions N/A is justified. Release with the condition that the per-account limit ships as committed.

DELETE /api/internal/users/[id] only requires a valid session and is outside the middleware's /api/admin matcher, so any signed-in member can permanently delete any user account. It needs an admin role check, or the route should move under /api/admin.

No release-blocking issues: the webhook verifies the Stripe signature, upgrades only paid sessions (including async payment success), and records the event ID in the same transaction as the upgrade, so duplicates are ignored and failures roll back for retry.

Checkout offers asynchronous methods (Bacs Direct Debit, customer_balance), but the webhook grants the pro plan on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status, so accounts are upgraded before or without payment. The event is also marked as processed before the update runs, outside a transaction, so a failed update is never retried.

The allow-list is a plain string-prefix check (url.startsWith("https://images.partner-cdn.com")), so hosts such as images.partner-cdn.com.attacker.net or userinfo tricks pass. Combined with redirect: "follow" and no size or content-type limits, this is a server-side request forgery (SSRF) that can fetch internal resources and store them as the avatar.

The audit confirms a high-severity finding (AG-004: password reset tokens never expire, and a two-day-old token was accepted). Accepting it as a risk with a next-sprint fix is not appropriate for an account-takeover vector, so the team's GO should not stand.

No code defect found, but the critical ownership check was run against commit 7fd543e rather than the audited release commit 43a2f97, which changed src/routes.py. The evidence for that critical check is stale and must be re-run before GO.

document_preview is SECURITY DEFINER with no owner filter and is executable by every authenticated user, so it bypasses RLS and returns the title and first 280 characters of any document by ID. It needs to filter on owner_id = auth.uid() or run as SECURITY INVOKER.

No code defect found, but the critical ownership, tenant-isolation and payment-verification checks are recorded as PASS from the commands `true` and `echo tenant isolation verified`, which test nothing. The evidence is fabricated or invalid, so GO cannot be recorded.

The transfer amount is never checked to be positive or finite, so a negative amount moves money from the recipient to the sender. That lets any user drain other wallets. Validate amount > 0 (and reject NaN/Infinity and bad precision); also lock both wallets in a consistent order to avoid deadlocks.

No code defect found, but the critical tenant-isolation check relies only on a static code read, with no command or exit code, and the read describes organisation scoping that the code (owner_id filtering) does not contain. A critical check without runtime evidence blocks GO.

No release-blocking issues: the invoice lookup goes through the Prisma extension, which forces userId = session.userId on findFirst, so users cannot read other users' invoices. Note that other invoice operations (findUnique, update, delete) are not scoped if they are added later.

The client input is spread after the server-side product fields ({ name, unitAmount, ...input }), so a request can override unitAmount and name and buy any product at an arbitrary price. Copy only quantity and note from the input, and validate quantity as an integer.
